turns.answer_text:
SHG is allowed in every pool structure (all are non-centrosymmetric), so the front is set by chemistry and polar alignment, not by inversion symmetry. Miller’s rule plus anionic-group theory gives a strongly convex (|d|, Eg) curve: light ionic salts at high Eg / small d, tetrahedral II–VI in the middle, and covalent pnictides/tellurides at low Eg / huge d. Five mutually non-dominated points were chosen along that curve, not five analogs of the same selenide.

- **c030 (CdSiP2, I-42d)** — chalcopyrite II–IV–V2. Experimental prototype of the mid-gap star: Eg ≈ 2.45 eV with d36 ≈ 85 pm/V from SiP4/CdP4 bond-charge SHG. Ordinary sulfides/selenides sit below this point.
- **c055 (AlGaAs2, R3m)** — 6-layer polar 3m Al0.5Ga0.5As with every MX4 tetrahedron pointing the same way (wurtzite-like, not zincblende). III–V SHG is among the largest known (GaAs d14 ≈ 170 pm/V); Eg ≈ 1.8–2.1 eV. Larger |d| than CdSiP2 at a still-open gap.
- **c037 (BeSe, F-43m)** — zincblende II–VI, Be–Se = 2.24 Å, V/atom = 17.4 Å³. Indirect Eg ≈ 4.5 eV (direct ~5.2 eV) with d14 typically 20–30 pm/V. Dominates LiAlS2, SiC, ZnGa2S4 and the thioborates on both axes or by the 1/Eg³ envelope.
- **c073 (CdIn3Te4As, P1)** — closed-shell tetrahedral CdTe/In2Te3/InAs alloy. Smallest-gap covalent semiconductor in the pool (~0.8–1.2 eV) with In–As/Te bonds of the same family as CdGeAs2/InAs (record bulk |d|). This is the high-|d| end; a metal would not be closed-shell here.
- **c068 (Sr4Br6O, P6_3mc)** — polar 6mm Sr4OBr6 with OSr4 tetrahedra aligned along c. Oxide–bromide without d10 or lone-pair cations, so Eg ≈ 5–6 eV, among the widest in the pool, with a finite d33 from the polar oxide tetrahedra. Needed so the set actually reaches the wide-gap axis rather than clustering on phosphides.

Together these five are chemically distinct (phosphide chalcopyrite, polar III–V, II–VI zincblende, Te/As tetrahedral alloy, polar oxide–bromide) and sit at well-separated Eg. That spans the dominated hypervolume; five Li–Mg–Ga–Se clones would not.

Final: c030, c055, c037, c073, c068
